$comment: Places that read a setting where the settings registry generator cannot take the key or the fallback from the call itself. Each entry is matched by file and a fragment of the line (code); an entry that matches nothing is an error, so moved or changed code shows up in --check.

places — calls of a reader (Settings.get/str/effective, the authcheck and edge-sync readers) with a computed key or a fallback that is not a literal. selector — the keys that reach this place: keys, category, prefix, policy (fields of the policy row), rows (the seed rows by the flags secret / required, in any category), edge_meta_keys, const (+ field/fields/index/values, prefix) and any (union); {"all": true} — any key (listed once under generic_reads). wrapper — a local helper that does the read: its calls (callee, key_arg, fallback_arg or a fixed fallback, prefix; scope — the enclosing block unless "file") become the places. extra — a reader the scanner does not see as a call (a map lookup inside a reader class). skip — a pass-through or a definition, with the reason.

getters — plain calls with a literal key of a getter the caller passes in (file + callee): the note says which readers stand behind it. ignore — calls that take a key but do not read its value (validation of a candidate, a log label). sql — statements over the settings table or its views whose keys are not literal (selector) or that read only metadata (skip). The scanner takes the keys of a statement only from a condition it parses completely (a conjunction of category = 'x', key = 'y', key IN ('a', …), path = 'c.k', NOT secret; other conjuncts only narrow the rows); any other condition needs an entry here with the full key list (selector) and the condition pinned as text (condition: a changed condition fails --check); nth — which of several mentions of the relation on that line.

reader — a kind from registry.json readers; fallback / fallback_by_key / fallback_const — what the place passes; fallback_from: caller — the fallback is passed by the caller and not known here; note / note_by_key — the place's own handling.

rule / rule_by_key — the same handling in machine form, applied by the snapshot tool after the reader, in order: absent, null, type+else, int, integer (not an integer → its value), min, max, number, positive, int_clamp+else, int_in+else (an integer in the range, otherwise else), in+else, eq, trim, edge_bound (out of the key's EDGE_RANGES bound) and out_of_range (another JSON type than the place's fallback, or out of the bound; both with an optional else for a value inside), unmodelled (a check that is not modelled: said in the snapshot), min_of (Math.min with the value the same place computes for another key, by that key's reader and rule: the other key must have a place on the same line) ("$fallback" — this place's fallback, "$strict" — its strict value, "$default_value" — the row's default_value, no row: null). not_modelled / not_modelled_by_key — what the real reader also depends on and the snapshot does not compute (another key, data, an argument): the snapshot shows the value without it, says so at the place and keeps the place out of the claim that it equals the reader. A note or via that names such a dependency (a closed list of words: at most / at least not followed by a number, the larger / stricter … of, least / greatest / min / max(, Math.min / max, depends on, derived, over all instances, largest / smallest; in a note also another key) fails --check unless the rule executes it (min_of) or the place is not_modelled. strict — how the place's strict value of a key is found (constants of fixed values, of the side of the integer bound and of defaults). requires — whole lines of the code the rule models on other lines (a helper): a changed line fails --check. A wrapper with a fixed fallback must match the literal of its inner reader call on the definition line, or name the wrapper it reads through in fallback_via; each call of a wrapper with a computed key is an entry of places with the wrapper's callee (a selector or skip).

Every SQL file of the tree is scanned (including the rollback files, the checks, the edge database, deploy/** — but deploy/data, sources.mjs SQL_SKIP_DIRS, and every top-level folder whose name begins with an underscore), and the SQL of deploy/** shell scripts, and the SQL in the strings of the script files of tools/** (.mjs, .cjs, .js; excluding directories named test and tools/deploy-tests, sources.mjs TOOL_SKIP_NAMES and TOOL_SKIP_DIRS); edge:meta — a reader of edge_meta.settings by name (keys listed in the selector).

edge_meta — the edge side (packages/edge-*/src, packages/bridge/src, contracts/schema/edge/** and contracts/schema/rollback/edge/**): every mention of a name of v_edge_export_settings that is not in the body of an edge:meta reader of places (its selector must hold the key) and not a metaInt(…, "name", literal) call is matched here by file and a fragment of the line (in SQL — of the statement), names (default: every name there) and form; reader/fallback/rule/note — a read of the key; skip — not a read, with the reason; export — the exporter shapes the value on its way to edge_meta (registry keys[…].edge_meta.export). A computed index of a settings object there is matched the same way and may only be a skip.

sql_mentions — the catch-all of SQL: every mention of the settings table or a view over it in SQL text (every SQL file of the tree, deploy/** shell, SQL strings of packages/*/src and of the script files of tools/** — decoded) that is not the relation of a read the scanner parses (FROM, JOIN, USING, a FROM list) and not a write or a definition it recognizes (sources.mjs classifyMention: INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE that do not read the stored row and whose statement ends in the same text — a write that goes on after a substitution or a + is not attributed; CREATE/ALTER/DROP, GRANT/REVOKE, an index, a trigger, COMMENT, REFERENCES) is matched here by file and a fragment of its line (found on exactly one line) and must say in skip why it is not a read; anything else fails --check.
